chapters.title: The math of brick-and-mortar bakery has stopped working.
chapters.body_html:
The rent on a typical Pune designer-cake outlet has climbed from ₹50,000 to ₹90,000 a month over the last few years, and real estate has not finished climbing. Yet a designer cake still sells at roughly ₹500, and that number is not flexible. A parent buying a child's birthday cake will not pay ₹900; the social ceiling for a family-occasion cake in Pune sits between ₹500 and ₹700. For a five-shopfront bakery, the rent gap alone is over ₹2,00,000 of fixed cost a month that the cake price cannot absorb.

This is not a bad quarter for the category. Rent in Pune moves in one direction. A designer cake's price is anchored to what a household considers reasonable for an occasion. The two lines do not meet again. Every renewal cycle widens the gap, and every new outlet inherits the same arithmetic. The squeeze is structural - it lives in the shape of the brick-and-mortar bakery model, not in a season or a slowdown.

The honest read is that the storefront model for designer cake in Pune has eighteen to thirty-six months of viable runway, and any operator paying close attention to monthly P&L can feel it. The question worth sitting with is not how to defend the shopfronts. It is what a designer-cake bakery looks like when the shopfronts are no longer the unit of the business.
The format is ending. The bakery model itself does not have to.

chapters.title: What if Fantasy ran without a single shopfront?
chapters.body_html:
Picture one central kitchen producing every cake fresh after the order arrives. Around it, a network of 25 to 40 fridge nodes placed inside neighbourhood kirana stores and dark-kitchen partners across Pune, each renting shelf-space for a few thousand rupees a month. A customer places an order on a Fantasy website with a four-hour lead time. The kitchen produces fresh, the cake travels to the nearest node, a delivery partner picks it up on a scheduled round, and it reaches the door the same day it was made.

The freshness story stops being a marketing line and becomes a property of the model. Most cake bought from a display counter today has been sitting one to two days; the customer cannot tell, but the bakery can. When the kitchen and the customer are linked by the order itself, no cake waits days on a shelf. Fantasy delivers a measurably fresher product, and does it at a lower delivered cost than carrying five shopfronts. That is a better cake and a healthier business at the same time.

The piece that makes this future feasible is not the kitchen and not the fridges. It is the layer that teaches a Pune parent to order four hours ahead instead of walking into a shop. A Fantasy website built for the four-hour rhythm, paired with a WhatsApp marketing engine that nudges occasions, reorders, and node-level offers, is the operating system of the new bakery. Without it, the model stays a diagram. With it, the model runs.

chapters.title: A custom web app, built for cakes, ready for the network.
chapters.body_html: The web app is the operating system for the new model. It collects orders four hours ahead, routes each one from the central kitchen to the nearest fridge node, and hands it to a delivery partner on a scheduled round. Every screen below exists to protect freshness, compress cost, and shift the customer from walk-in-and-grab to order-and-receive-fresh.

chapters.title: Teaching a city to plan four hours ahead.
chapters.body_html:
The new model only works if Pune parents learn one small habit: order four hours ahead. Every other piece of the system - the central kitchen, the fridge nodes, the partner network - is already engineered. The single missing variable is consumer behaviour. Marketing is therefore not decoration on this rollout. It is the structural unlock. Without a steady drumbeat reaching the right households at the right moments of the week, the freshness advantage stays invisible and the model stays underused. With it, the four-hour window quietly becomes the new normal for designer cakes in Pune.

Jarvis Daily runs that drumbeat end-to-end on WhatsApp. Four to six broadcasts a month, written and scheduled by us, teach the four-hour habit through festive campaigns, weekend cravings, and seasonal launches. Birthday and anniversary auto-flows reach customers a week ahead, when the decision is actually being made. Cart-abandonment nudges recover orders that stalled mid-checkout. Every customer reply lands inside Fantasy's dashboard as a tagged lead, ready for the team to close. Fantasy approves the calendar; we operate it.

Our central kitchen begins it the moment your order arrives, and it reaches you in just 4 hours. That short wait is the reason every Fantasy cake tastes the way it does. Try it this weekend. Order by 2 PM, celebrate by 6 PM.

That is why our buttercream still tastes like cream and our sponge still tastes like the morning. If you have not ordered from us in a while, this is your reminder.

Our unicorn-and-pastel collection is open for booking, with custom toppers, names piped in gold, and the four-hour fresh promise you already know us for. Reply with the date and the flavour, and we will hold the slot.

chapters.title: Scope, FAQ, and what each side owns.
chapters.body_html:
What is not included in this engagement. Native iOS or Android apps (future expansion). Multi-city operations beyond Pune (future expansion). A separate kirana-partner mobile app for fridge-node operators (future Phase 2). Direct integration with restaurant-OS platforms (orders flow through admin for now). Razorpay merchant onboarding (Fantasy holds the merchant account directly). Studio photography or content creation outside AI-generated assets.

Frequent questions.

Why ₹20,000/month when SaaS platforms cost ₹3,000?
A SaaS template gives you a generic restaurant page. No central-kitchen routing, no fridge-node inventory, no four-hour freshness passport, no managed WhatsApp campaigns, no path to the kirana-fridge model. Our retainer replaces a part-time marketing manager (₹25,000-30,000/month) and keeps your custom platform running. Stop paying any time and the system still belongs to you.

What does the setup actually cover?
Roughly 600 hours of skilled work over 8-10 weeks: design, custom development, AI integration, WhatsApp Business API setup, Meta template approvals, testing, deployment, and onboarding for your team.

How does the kirana-fridge network roll out?
The web app is built with multi-fulfilment-point architecture from day one - the data model already understands multiple distribution nodes. We launch with the central kitchen plus the first 5-10 fridge partners. Adding nodes 11 through 40 happens through admin UI without engineering work. The kirana-partner mobile app is a future Phase 2 add-on, not a rebuild.

Who pays for WhatsApp messages and AI API usage?
Fantasy pays Meta and OpenAI directly through accounts set up in your name during onboarding. We never resell those bills. Estimated combined external cost: ₹6,000 to ₹8,000/month at typical bakery volume.

What if my volume grows beyond what the retainer covers?
The retainer covers up to 500 orders/month of support load. Beyond that, we either tier up the retainer transparently or move you to Phase 2 (multi-kitchen routing engine, designed for higher volume).

Can I see the platform before paying everything?
Yes. After kickoff (₹1,50,000), you see working screens within two weeks and a fully working UAT version before the second payment. The third and final payment only happens after you have personally confirmed go-live success.

Data Ownership and Intellectual Property.
chapters.body_after_animation_html:
Your data is yours. All customer records, order history, transaction logs, WhatsApp conversation history, customer database, and analytics belong entirely to Fantasy Bakery 'n' Patisserie. You receive full administrative access to view, export, and delete this data at any time. Jarvis Daily will not use your customer or order data for any purpose other than operating your platform. On termination, Jarvis Daily provides a complete export within seven business days.

Our platform is ours. The bot software, source code, system prompts, AI instructions, content generation templates, marketing workflows, admin dashboard codebase, and underlying infrastructure remain the intellectual property of Jarvis Daily. Fantasy Bakery is licensing the use of this platform and the operational service around it, not acquiring ownership of the platform itself. This is standard practice for managed software services and protects our ability to keep improving the platform across all clients.

Third-party services operate under their own terms. The platform uses industry-standard third-party services: Razorpay for payments, Meta's WhatsApp Business API for messaging, OpenAI and Google for AI image and text generation, and a cloud hosting provider for infrastructure. Each operates under its own terms and retains records per its own policies. Razorpay records are retained as required under Indian tax and payments regulation, independent of this SOW. Jarvis Daily selects responsible providers but does not warrant third-party conduct or uptime. Total liability for any sub-processor incident is capped at fees paid in the preceding three months.
